My cents:

Stefan wrote:

> i played in the ne qualifier this year and finished 3rd with 1 gw and
> 5.5 vps. 40 player
> participated in the qualifier i recieved 98 points.
> at gencon i played the final qualifier with 90 players participating.
> i finished 5 with 2 gw and 8 vps but only recieved 79 points.

NE qualifier: 3 out of 40 with 1 GWs and 5.5 VPs. Objectively he was
better than 37 participants. Relatively he scored in the upper 7.5%.

GenCon: 5 out of 90 players with 2 GWs and 8 VPs. Objectively he was
better than 85 participants. Relatively he scored in the upper 5.5%.

That should probably mean that he should gain more Rank Points for the
GenCon performance. "Besting" 85 players seems harder than "besting" 37.
Accumulating 2/8 seems harder than accumulating 1/5.5.

I think that in general the closer you get to one end of the distribution
of the participants, the more indicative the distance from the other end
will become (as opposed to how humans frequently view it). Scoring 5th
place in the preliminaries is very different from scoring sixth, yet in a
tournament with 90 players the objective performance is likely almost
identical - "besting" 85 or 84 people is a very small difference. Same
with the low end: scoring last is in for a "lemon" prize, but being 89th
or 90th is quite an insignificant difference.

Most representative of performance is perhaps the actual GW/VP scored,
regardless of any position. Or the number of players who were "bested". In
my opinion, of course. ;)

Bye,

Daneel

This is all true, sure. Before the current system went into place, I
argued for a scoring method that ran a little more linearly (or on a
curve, really) from 1st place down to 50th (or whatever last happens to
actually be), but what we ended up with is a system that weights making
the finals much more highly than anything else. Everyone here has read
the scoring system page, right? :-)

http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/index.php?line=veknRating.html

The bonus points for placing between 1st and 5th in a tournament are
very significant to overall points earned - especially in larger
tournaments, because the size-coefficient on points earned applies to
the finalist bonus but not to the standardized "points for VPs, points
for GWs" earned in all rounds. For example, you get 10 points for 5th
(times the size coefficient) but 30 for 3rd (again, times the size
coefficient) and 90 for 1st (still multiplied by the size coefficient).

That's why 3rd is normally going to score better than 5th, even if the
5th is at a significantly larger tournament than the 3rd was.

I don't think this system is significantly flawed relative to many other
ways it could be done. I do, as you say, think that it would make more
sense to slope the points earned down past the finalists more, but given
that tournaments have always been played with a "finals are the most
important game" system, it does make some sense for the finalists to
earn substantially more points than non-finalists.

Josh

Messages.Author: Curevei
Messages.Body:
>That should probably mean that he should gain more Rank Points for the
>GenCon performance. "Besting" 85 players seems harder than "besting" 37.
>Accumulating 2/8 seems harder than accumulating 1/5.5.

As placement already factors GWs and VPs, it's not necessary to double count
them. The current system only minimally double counts them, well, compared to
what you get for making the finals, at least. If you don't make the finals,
it's your entire score.

You can't accurately compare absolute numbers between tournaments which is why
the previous system was so ludicrous. Could, for instance, have two 40 player
tournaments where one sees no time outs and lots of sweeps because the players'
skills are so uneven and the other sees lots of time outs and table splits
because the players' skills are so close. Actually, it doesn't matter why you
see one or the other, but these are not unreasonable reasons as to why you
might see this difference. Placement can't take into account the total skill
of all players in the event, but it fully takes into account, to the extent
that any rating system that will be used is likely to do so, relative skill for
the event. (Which is kind of why I'd rather see placement be the primary
scoring method for everyone.)

Now, getting back to a possible flaw, it could be that 3rd shouldn't count any
more than 5th as players don't think that much in terms of coming in 3rd.
Going to depend upon prize allocations, but sometimes players won't value 2nd
any more than 5th. My sense is that people, looking from the outside, mostly
care about 1) did the person make the final table 2) did the person win.

And, sure, somewhat getting back to the thing about beating more players, you
do get kind of screwed if you don't make the final table. Stefan's result may
be the problem of valuing 3rd and 5th so differently, but whoever came in 6th
in either event probably deserves a lot more since they both beat large numbers
of players where being 6th in a 15 player tournament (apparently the standard
for the point system) is not nearly as impressive.

I don't understand why pure placement couldn't be used. But, recalling the
hassle that was instituting the latest fix and the mindnumbing uselessness of
the previous system, I could see not worrying that much about this problem.

always host 5 people, while the number of participants may be quite

actually means that in order to maintain a good rating, you have to go to

latter is rated far lower.

The VP and GW counting component is an excellent idea, by the way. For the
other part of the rating though I could probably imagine something that
has more to do with tournament ranking in general than giving bonuses for
making the finals (which is further strengthening the differences between

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
"Daneel" <dan...@eposta.hu> wrote in message

> > I don't think this system is significantly flawed relative to
> > many other ways it could be done.
>

> this is a fairly general statement... ;)

I think what Josh is trying to say, here, is that it's kind of
silly to quibble about the "fairness" of a system like this. A
system based on granting players points for showing up at
tournaments (whether it's JUST for showing up or whether you actually
have to do something once you're there is ultimately irrelevant)
is not fair in terms of rating players skills and never will be.
Steve Wieck termed this a "rewards" system because it rewards players
for participating and ultimately chose it because it's more
popular (and quite possibly more understandable) than ELO or
any other scheme purported to actually rate players' skill
mathematically from demonstrated results.

You show up at a tournament, you get some points for doing well.
Your little number that you can go look up on the web reflects a
set of these rewards point showings earned in the last 18 months.
Enjoy. Have fun with it, for what it's worth. But let's not
pretend one scheme or another makes more sense.

Fred

At this point? Just not worrying about it. I don't aim to dredge
up arguments about ELO at this point, if that's what you're concerned
about. I'm just pointing out that you have to do _something_ like
ELO in order to have any hope of accurately rating player skill.

> unlike chess, vampire is not a duel type game and has a lot to do
> with luck. You can beat the #1 Vtes player if you sit at his table
> because of his poor drawing and using cross table interaction.
> You cannot beat the #1 chess player by luck or manipulating
> someone else.

Sure. I agree, these make it more challenging to construct a
mathematical way of rating players in V:tES. Perhaps they make it
impossible, I can't say. The one time we tried it, we chose
coefficients that were brainlessly broken and no one paid attention
or bothered to notice this for two years. (In retrospect, that was
really dumb of us all, IMHO. I knew _something_ was wrong - but I
just *assumed* whoever had proposed the system was bothering to
watch how it worked. Guess that was naive...) It may well be that
if we chose good ones, we'd get reasonable numbers out of the thing.
But I agree, it doesn't seem likely we'd ever get anything as
dependable as chess ratings.

> Does it mean the whole idea of rating vtes players should be
> flushed away ?

I'm not sure what this question is getting at. If you mean, can
we ever bang *THIS* system into one that will accurately rate
player? Heavens, no! It doesn't even begin to do the right things.
As I said in the other post, it's a *reward*-based system that
gives you points (or the opportunity for points) as a reward for
showing up. The basis on which it grants points to players is
non-existant. Basically, we'll give some quantity of points to
players that have done things that _sound_ good. Who knows if
it's the right number?

But why worry about it? It's a system for assigning bragging
rights, nothing more. People probably find it fun to go look up
their numbers after they've been granted some points. If that's
some fun (and I won't deny looking up mine, either), then so be
it. Just, let's not get too passionate about arguing what the
"right" number of points for each acheivement turns out to be.

Fred
